text: Play on the a-file
zh: a线上的战斗

text: We have chosen as the basic theme the question of planning play along the a-file, when it occurs with castling king's side by both opponents. Namely these cases of play along the a-file assume a specific character, requiring an independent examination.
zh: 我们选取双方均已短易位时围绕a线展开的计划性行棋作为基本主题。这类a线行动具有鲜明特点，值得单独研究。

text: What features characterise play along the a-file, with king's side castling by both sides? Firstly, the a-file is as distant as can be from the king's flank, as a result of which the principal events, for the time being, do not affect the castled positions. Even more important is the fact that the side holding the initiative in play on the a-file must concentrate large-scale forces, and in any case the rooks, on that file or near it. It means that such play is attended by the diversion of important pieces from the king's flank. But this could prompt the opponent to direct his forces to an attack there, in the event of which it is very important to take care of the defence of the king's flank with a solid pawn chain and a minor piece covering detachment.
zh:
双方均在王翼易位时，a线行动具有哪些特点？首先，a线与王翼相距甚远，所以主要战事暂时不会直接影响易位后的王城。更重要的是，掌握a线主动权的一方必须在该线及其附近集中大量兵力，尤其是双车。这意味着重要棋子会被调离王翼，从而可能促使对手转而进攻王翼。因此，必须以稳固兵链和少量轻子妥善守护王翼。

译注：从残局的观点来看，由于a线距离王城非常远，而轻子对于通路兵，尤其是边线通路兵的防守能力较弱，如果在此处的战斗发生大量重子兑换，后翼一旦出现通路兵将是决定性的。在围绕a线斗争的过程中执行兑换或者兵的突破时，必须时刻考虑到这一点。

text: The technique of opening the a-file consists of the exchange of the a-pawn for the b-pawn. Such an exchange is difficult to achieve if the b-pawn stands on its original square. Therefore it is useful, as a pre-requisite to opening the a-file, to provoke the advance of the knight's pawn one or two squares. There is no need to mention that the plan of opening the a-file and the future invasion on it must be carefully thought out, taking into account all the concrete positional conditions, to weigh up whether it is possible for the opponent to advantageously prevent the opening of the a-file or launch a successful counter-attack on the king's flank.
zh: 打开a线的基本方法，是以a兵交换对方的b兵。如果b兵仍在初始格，这种交换便难以实现。因此，打开a线之前，往往要先诱使对方的b兵冲起一格或两格。不言而喻，打开a线并随后沿线侵入的计划必须经过周密考虑：既要结合局面的具体条件，也要权衡对手能否有利地阻止开线，或在王翼发动有效反击。

text: In planning play on the a-file, it is of course necessary to secure the occupation of the opened line with his rooks. It means that an appropriate regrouping of forces must take place even before the opening of the line.
zh: 规划a线行动时，当然必须确保开线后能够以双车占据该线。这意味着适当的子力重组必须在a线打开之前便已完成。

text: As an excellent example of the technique of invasion on the a-file might serve the ending of the game Marco-Muller, played as long ago as the end of the last century (1898) in the accessory tournament of the international congress in London.
zh: 早在十九世纪末的伦敦国际象棋大会附属赛（1898年）中，马尔科对穆勒一局的收尾，便出色展示了沿a线侵入的技术。

text: White has prepared the opening and occupation of the a-file.
zh: 白方已经为打开并占据a线做好准备。

text: Now an immediate capture on b6 was also not bad. After 33. axb6 axb6 34. Qa1! Rxa4 35. Rxa4 the a-file would be in White's hands, which, in connection with the weakness of the b6 and e6 pawns, must in the end decide the game in his favour. And yet the reply 35... Rd7 would have allowed Black to defend himself quite tenaciously.
zh: 此时立即在b6吃兵也不坏。白方若走33. axb6 axb6 34. Qa1! Rxa4 35. Rxa4，便可掌握a线；结合b6兵和e6兵的弱点，这最终应当为白方带来胜利。不过，黑方以35... Rd7回应后仍可顽强防守。

text: Marco chose the best possibility:
zh: 马尔科选择了最佳下法：

text:
**33. Qa1!**

 only now threatening axb6. In order not to lose a pawn, Black is forced to take the rook away from the a8 square, after which White captures the a-file, retaining all the heavy pieces. There followed: 

**33... Rab8 34. axb6 axb6 35. Ra7+ Kh8 36. Rc7 Ra8 37. Raa7 Rxa7 38. Qxa7**
zh:
**33. Qa1!**

这时才真正威胁axb6。为了不丢兵，黑方被迫将a8车移开，随后白方便能在保留全部重子的情况下占据a线。实战接着走：

**33... Rab8 34. axb6 axb6 35. Ra7+ Kh8 36. Rc7 Ra8 37. Raa7 Rxa7 38. Qxa7**

text: White has doubled on the seventh rank and this predetermines a quick end.
zh: 白方在第七横线叠起重子，胜负很快便见分晓。

text: In this example there were quiet conditions on the king's flank. The locked pawn chain guarded the White king from any sort of trouble and he was able to transfer all his forces to the a-file.
zh: 在这个例子中，王翼局面很平稳。封闭的兵链使白王免受任何威胁，白方便能把全部子力调往a线。

text: In the game Lasker-Showalter (Nürnberg 1896) the overall situation was rather different. Black has succeeded in opening the a-file with the pawn march-route ...a5-a4xb3, captured it and invaded on the first and second ranks with his heavy pieces. Lasker endeavours to exploit as far as possible the time spent by Showalter on the whole of this operation, to create counter threats against the enemy king, which remains on h8 under cover of the pawn chain h7-g6-f5 and the knight e6. After White's 60th move this strategically interesting game arrived at the following position, which is not easy to evaluate.
zh: 在拉斯克对肖瓦尔特一局（纽伦堡，1896年）中，整体形势则大不相同。黑方通过...a5-a4xb3的冲兵路线成功打开并占据a线，随后以重子侵入第一、第二横线。拉斯克则力求利用肖瓦尔特为整套行动耗费的时间，对黑王制造反击威胁。黑王仍在h8，由h7-g6-f5兵链和e6马掩护。白方走完第60步后，这盘战略上颇有意思的对局形成了图示局面，其优劣并不容易判断。

text: Clouds hang over the White king but also White has his own chances. The splendidly placed knight on d5, transferring to f6, opens the h1-a8 diagonal for the queen. By penetrating on it to b7 or c6, he is able to create direct threats to the enemy king.
zh: 白王头顶乌云密布，但白方也有自己的机会。位置极佳的d5马转到f6后，便能为后打开h1-a8斜线。白后沿这条斜线侵入b7或c6，就能对黑王制造直接威胁。

text: There was a sharp and interesting development of events:
zh: 接下来，局势的发展既尖锐又有趣：

text:
With the threat ...Qf1. However Black does not foresee the opponent's dangerous counterattack. He could make a draw, but not more, by playing 61... Rg1+ 62. Bxg1 Qxg1+ 63. Kh3 Nxf4+ 64. Qxf4 Qh1+ 65. Kg3 Qg1+ 66. Kh3 Qh1+ etc. (67. Qh2 Qf1+). True, on 61... Rg1+ possible is 62. Kh2, but then 62... Rf1 63. Rd2 Qe1 leads to a complicated position in which Black can apparently defend himself. Now, however, there comes an immediate denouement. 

**62. Qb7 Ng7 63. Qf7 1-0**
zh:
威胁...Qf1。然而，黑方没有预见到对手危险的反击。他本可通过61... Rg1+ 62. Bxg1 Qxg1+ 63. Kh3 Nxf4+ 64. Qxf4 Qh1+ 65. Kg3 Qg1+ 66. Kh3 Qh1+等后续手段求和，但也仅此而已（67. Qh2 Qf1+）。当然，对61... Rg1+，白方也可走62. Kh2；不过，62... Rf1 63. Rd2 Qe1会形成复杂局面，黑方看来能够守住。实战中，胜负却立即揭晓：

**62. Qb7 Ng7 63. Qf7 1-0**

text: Could Black, instead of 60... Rb1, have played stronger? 60... Qc1 offered chances of a win. If 61. Nf6 then 61... Qc2 and there is only one more for White - the return of the knight to d5, since on 62. Bg1 follows 62... Qg2+. Black's further plan is this: to exchange queens by playing 62... Qe2, return the rook to b2 (in the event of 63. Qxe2), transfer the king to f7 and dispatch the knight to a5 to win the b3 pawn. Several instructive examples of play on the a-file can be found in the creative work of Capablanca.
zh: 黑方能否用更强的走法替代60... Rb1？60... Qc1可以争取胜机。若61. Nf6，则61... Qc2，白方只有把马退回d5，因为62. Bg1会遭到62... Qg2+。黑方接下来的计划是走62... Qe2兑后；若63. Qxe2，就把车撤回b2，再把王调到f7，马调到a5，以吃掉b3兵。在卡帕布兰卡的对局中，我们还可以找到几个富有启发性的a线作战范例。

text: In a game with Treybal (Carlsbad 1929), Capablanca, playing White, after a protracted siege of the enemy position, succeeded, by locking the centre and the king's flank, in opening the a-file and invading on it with the heavy pieces.
zh: 在对特雷巴尔的一局中（卡尔斯巴德，1929年），执白的卡帕布兰卡经过长时间围攻，封闭了中心和王翼，成功打开a线，并以重子沿线侵入。

text: White easily controls the a-file. Black, locked up by White's powerful black-squared seven-pawn chain, is obliged to stick to waiting tactics. The only question is whether White can exploit the inevitable invasion of his rook on a7.
zh: 白方轻而易举地控制着a线。他的七个兵组成强大的黑格兵链，把黑方牢牢封锁住，迫使黑方只能等待。唯一的问题在于：白车侵入a7已不可阻止，但白方能否利用这一点取得成果？

text: The game continued:
zh: 实战接着走：

text: 40. Ra1 Rc8
zh: 40. Ra1 Rc8

text: Useless is 40... Qa8 41. Qb2.
zh: 40... Qa8 41. Qb2也无济于事。

text: 41. Qb4 Rhd8 42. Ra7 Kf8 43. Rhh1 Be8 44. Rha1 Kg8 45. R1a4 Kf8 46. Qa3 Kg8
zh: 41. Qb4 Rhd8 42. Ra7 Kf8 43. Rhh1 Be8 44. Rha1 Kg8 45. R1a4 Kf8 46. Qa3 Kg8

text: White has invaded, placing his heavy pieces on the a-file in an ideal order with the queen behind, but... what next? The following manoeuvre with the king testifies to the fact that Capablanca has still not put together a clear plan of action.
zh: 白方已经侵入，并将重子以理想的次序配置在a线上，后居于双车之后。然而，下一步该怎么办？接下来的运王表明，卡帕布兰卡尚未形成明确的行动计划。

text: 47. Kg3 Bd7 48. Kh4 Kh8 49. Qa1 Kg8 50. Kg3
zh: 47. Kg3 Bd7 48. Kh4 Kh8 49. Qa1 Kg8 50. Kg3

text: The king was poorly placed on h4; after the removal of the White knight from f3, there could arise the motive of a sacrifice on g5.
zh: 王在h4的位置不佳；白马一旦离开f3，黑方便可能获得在g5弃子的战术机会。

text: Everything becomes clear. Black has a weak pawn on b7; the White knight is headed for a5.
zh: 现在，一切都清楚了。黑方的b7兵是弱兵，白马正准备转往a5。

text: 52... Bd7 53. Nb3 Re8 54. Na5 Nd8 55. Ba6! bxa6 56. Rxd7
zh: 52... Bd7 53. Nb3 Re8 54. Na5 Nd8 55. Ba6! bxa6 56. Rxd7

text: The seventh rank is included in the zone of invasion.
zh: 白方的侵入范围扩展到了第七横线。

text: It is apparent from the ending that the rook on a7 gave defensive help to the minor pieces. The question arises whether White would have been able to exploit his enormous advantage in space on the a-file if there were only heavy pieces on the board? Alas, no. He would have nothing with which to attack the b7 pawn.
zh: 从这段收尾可以看出，a7车为轻子提供了防守上的支持。这便引出一个问题：如果棋盘上只有重子，白方还能利用自己在a线上的巨大空间优势吗？恐怕不能，因为他将没有合适的棋子去攻击b7兵。

text: A good reply to this question might be gleaned from the concluding part of the 25th game of the 1927 world championship match, Capablanca-Alekhine.
zh: 1927年卡帕布兰卡对阿廖欣世界冠军赛第25局的收尾，可以很好地回答这个问题。

text: 26. b5 axb5
zh: 26. b5 axb5

text: Forced, otherwise White himself exchanges on a6 and invades on the b-file.
zh: 这是被迫的，否则白方会主动在a6交换，再沿b线侵入。

text: 27. axb5
zh: 27. axb5

text: On the face of it, it seems that the a-file will even be occupied by Black, but this is only a semblance.
zh: 乍看之下，似乎反而是黑方会占据a线，但这只是表象。

text: Anticipating future events, Alekhine forces an exchange of the last minor pieces in order to make easier the subsequent defence of the b7 pawn.
zh: 阿廖欣预见到接下来的局势发展，强制交换双方最后的轻子，以便随后更容易地防守b7兵。

text: 28. Bxg6 Qxg6 29. Ra1 Rac8
zh: 28. Bxg6 Qxg6 29. Ra1 Rac8

text:
On 29... Rcc8 White would win a pawn by replying 30. Rxa8 Rxa8 31. Qb6. 

**30. b6 Rd7 31. Ra7 Kh7 32. Rca1 f5 33. Qc2 Re7 34. g3 Rce8**
zh:
若29... Rcc8，白方以30. Rxa8 Rxa8 31. Qb6即可得兵。

**30. b6 Rd7 31. Ra7 Kh7 32. Rca1 f5 33. Qc2 Re7 34. g3 Rce8**

text: Black, for the present, does not threaten anything on the e-file, but also White cannot increase the pressure on the b7 pawn.
zh: 黑方暂时无法在e线上制造威胁，但白方也无法进一步增加对b7兵的压力。

text: Alekhine expressed the opinion that, instead of 26. b5, White should play at once 26. Ra1, in order to avoid the exchange of bishops. In this case he would have more chances of exploiting his advantage on the queen's flank, but retaining the bishops would also have increased the defensive resources of Black, who, moreover, because of the open character of the position, could organise counterplay in the centre and on the king's flank.
zh: 阿廖欣认为，白方应立即走26. Ra1，而不是26. b5，以避免兑象。这样，白方利用后翼优势的机会会更多；不过，保留双方的象也会增加黑方的防守资源。况且局面比较开放，黑方还可以在中心和王翼组织反击。

text: There is a sharper, but in return very keen, course of events when play on the a-file is countered with an initiative displayed by the opponent on the king's flank. At times play on the a-file will develop into a real counterattack, which, when combined with measures to defend one's own king, can bring decisive success, particularly when the opponent is too carried away by an attack on the king's flank.
zh: 当一方沿a线展开行动，而对手以王翼的主动行动相抗衡时，斗争就会变得更加尖锐激烈。有时，a线行动会发展为真正的反击；只要同时做好对己方王的防守，就可能取得决定性成果，尤其是在对手过分专注于王翼进攻的时候。

text: So let us return to practical material.
zh: 下面继续看实战例局。

text: Bird's Opening
zh: 伯德开局

text: White:P.Evtifeev
zh: 白方：P. 叶夫季费耶夫

text: Black: D.Danushevsky
zh: 黑方：D. 达努舍夫斯基

text: (Petersburg 1909)
zh: （圣彼得堡，1909年）

text: 1. f4 d5 2. e3 c5 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. b3 Nc6 5. Bb2 e6
zh: 1. f4 d5 2. e3 c5 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. b3 Nc6 5. Bb2 e6

text:
In this opening White's plan consists of the following: by firmly controlling the e5 square, to obtain a dominating position on the king's flank and then, by establishing a harmony of action between the bishop b2, queen and king's rook (O-O, Rf1-f3-g3 or h3), to launch a direct attack on the enemy king. From the point of view of countering this plan Black plays the opening, if not weakly, then inoffensively. One of the best possibilities for Black is the development of the bishop on g7. Therefore in place of 3... Nf6, worth considering is 3... g6. Likewise Black does not need to hurry with the development of the queen's knight, so as not to allow the pin with the bishop on b5 or first of all to prevent this pin by... a6. 

**6. Be2**
zh:
在这个开局中，白方的计划是牢牢控制e5格，从而在王翼取得主导地位，再让b2象、后及王翼车协调配合，对黑王发动直接进攻。王翼车的调动路线是短易位后经f1-f3转到g3或h3。从对抗这一计划的角度看，黑方的开局下法即使谈不上软弱，也至少缺乏针对性。黑方较好的选择之一是把象出到g7，因此第3步值得考虑3... g6，而不是3... Nf6。同样，黑方也不必急于出后翼马，以免白象上b5形成牵制；或者先走...a6，防止这种牵制。

**6. Be2**

text: Undoubtedly, more consistent was 6. Bb5 with a subsequent exchange of the knight, which allows White to even more firmly consolidate himself on the central e5 point. We are time and again convinced of the need to link planning between the opening and central stage of the chess game.
zh: 毫无疑问，6. Bb5更符合白方的计划；随后以象换马，可以进一步巩固对中心e5格的控制。这再次说明，开局与中局的计划必须相互衔接。

text: 6... Be7 7. O-O O-O 8. Qe1 b6 9. Ne5
zh: 6... Be7 7. O-O O-O 8. Qe1 b6 9. Ne5

text: At least a premature thrust. Both now and on the following move he should prefer d3, since an exchange on e5 only plays into Black's hands.
zh: 这次跃马至少为时过早。无论现在还是下一步，白方都应优先考虑d3，因为在e5交换只会正中黑方下怀。

text:
Both opponents play not planned, but separate moves. Instead of 10. Qg3 it was necessary to play at first 10. d3, so as, on 10... d4, to have the reply e4. However, Black could exploit the favourable conditions and begin an offensive in the centre by... d4. Possibly, he feared 11. Bf3, but the following variation shows that there were no grounds at all for "fright": 11... Nd5 12. e4 Nxe5 13. fxe5 Nb4 14. Na3 a6 with a clear plan of a pawn advance on the queen's flank, or 12. Nxc6 Bxc6 13. exd4 (13. e4? Bh4 14. Qg4? f5 15. exf5 exf5 16. Bxd5+ Qxd5! with a decisive superiority) 13... Bh4 14. Qh3 Bf6 and Black obviously stands better and holds the initiative. The transfer of the knight from f6 to d6, and the bishop to f6, carried out instead of this, is also not bad, but it solves only one particular problem. 

**11. Qh3 Bf6 12. d3 Nd6 13. Nd2**
zh:
双方都没有按计划行棋，而是在各走各的零散招法。白方应先走10. d3，而不是10. Qg3，以便用e4应对10... d4。黑方本来也可以利用有利条件，以...d4在中心发动进攻。他可能担心11. Bf3，但下面的变化说明，这种顾虑完全没有必要：11... Nd5 12. e4 Nxe5 13. fxe5 Nb4 14. Na3 a6，黑方有明确的后翼冲兵计划；或者12. Nxc6 Bxc6 13. exd4（13. e4? Bh4 14. Qg4? f5 15. exf5 exf5 16. Bxd5+ Qxd5!，黑方取得决定性优势）13... Bh4 14. Qh3 Bf6，黑方明显占优并掌握主动。实战中，黑方选择把马从f6调到d6、把象调到f6，这也不坏，但只解决了一个局部问题。

**11. Qh3 Bf6 12. d3 Nd6 13. Nd2**

text: He should wait a little with this natural and even necessary move, which springs from concrete considerations. As will be seen from the note to Black's move in reply, it would have been very useful now to close down the f5 square for the opponent's knight by playing g4.
zh: 这步棋自然，甚至也是必要的，但从具体局面出发，白方应稍缓一步。对黑方下一步的分析将表明，此时先走g4，剥夺黑马利用f5格的可能，会非常有用。

text: Side by side with the 21st move, Black's most serious positional mistake in the present game. True, there is no denying that he has a certain planning for his game. He intends a broad pawn advance on the queen's flank, projecting it on the theme of play on the a-file. However, upon this, Black makes a very superficial calculation of White's attacking possibilities on the king's flank and, by eliminating the pawn tension in the centre himself with his last move, leaves White free to act in that sector of the board. This mistake must have fatal consequences.
zh: 与第21步一样，这是黑方本局最严重的局面错误之一。不可否认，黑方的行棋确有一定计划：他准备在后翼大举冲兵，围绕a线展开行动。然而，他对白方王翼进攻可能性的估计过于肤浅。这步棋主动消除了中心兵之间的紧张，使白方能够放手在王翼行动。这个错误本应带来致命后果。

text: Meanwhile, Black had at his disposal an interesting possibility - 13... Bxe5, and White has to think carefully before deciding how to recapture the bishop. If, for example, 14. Bxe5, then 14... Nxe5 15. fxe5 Nf5 and on 16. g4 follows 16... Qh4, while on 16. Bg4 good enough is 16... Nh6. The sacrifice of the exchange is doubtful in view of 17... Bc8 or 17... Qe7. The same consideration applies also to the variation 14. fxe5 Nf5, only in this situation the exchange sacrifice promises White rather more chances, since the bishop on b2 is still present, though after 15. Rxf5 exf5 16. Qxf5 Bc8 17. Qh5 Ne7 Black has quite a solid position.
zh: 其实，黑方有一个值得研究的选择：13... Bxe5。白方必须仔细考虑，究竟用什么吃回这只象。例如，14. Bxe5 Nxe5 15. fxe5 Nf5之后，16. g4可用16... Qh4应对；对白方的16. Bg4，16... Nh6也足够好。由于黑方有17... Bc8或17... Qe7，白方弃半子的效果值得怀疑。14. fxe5 Nf5这一变化也有类似情况，只是由于白方还保留着b2象，弃半子能够带来更多机会。不过，15. Rxf5 exf5 16. Qxf5 Bc8 17. Qh5 Ne7之后，黑方的局面仍相当稳固。

text: However, none of this happens and Black's game begins to go downhill.
zh: 实战没有出现上述变化，黑方的局面开始恶化。

text: 14. Nxc6 Bxc6 15. e4 e5
zh: 14. Nxc6 Bxc6 15. e4 e5

text: On top of everything else, admittedly already in the worse position, Black allows the opponent to cut off all his forces from the king's flank and develop an irresistible attack on the king. 15... Be7 was better.
zh: 黑方的局面原本已经较差，这一步又让对手能够切断黑方全部子力与王翼的联系，进而对王发动难以抵挡的进攻。15... Be7更好。

text: The bishop will invade on the third rank, but alas it turns out here to be only "a caliph for a day".
zh: 这只象即将侵入第三横线，可惜它在这里的威风只能是昙花一现。

text: 17. Nf3 Be3+ 18. Kh1 f6 19. Bc1 Bxc1
zh: 17. Nf3 Be3+ 18. Kh1 f6 19. Bc1 Bxc1

text: Black cannot hold his ground on e3. For example, 19... Nb5 20. Ng1, attacking the bishop again with the queen.
zh: 黑象无法在e3站稳脚跟。例如19... Nb5 20. Ng1，白方又能用后攻击这只象。

text: 20. Raxc1 b5
zh: 20. Raxc1 b5

text: Black begins to carry out his plan of attack on the queen's flank. On an immediate 20... a5 could follow 21. a4. But now he intends to take the route-march ...a5-a4xb3. However, White's attack must achieve its objective quicker.
zh: 黑方开始实施后翼进攻计划。如果立即走20... a5，白方可以21. a4回应；现在黑方准备按...a5-a4xb3的路线冲兵。不过，白方的进攻本应更快奏效。

text:
In pursuit of beautiful incidental threats, like Ng6, White makes an incorrect assessment of the position. You see, he cannot break the defensive line of Black pawns on the king's flank with just a one-piece attack. White chooses an unrealistic plan, his idea is not sufficiently concrete. He should, however, play 21. g4 and if 21... Nf7, then 22. Qg3. There might then follow: 22... h6 23. h4 a5 24. Rf2 a4 25. Rg1 axb3 26. axb3 Ra2 27. g5! hxg5 28. hxg5 Rxc2 29. Rh2 fxg5 30. Qh3 Nh6 31. Rxg5 with numerous threats.

**21... Be8**
zh:
白方一味追求Ng6之类漂亮的临时威胁，对局面作出了错误判断。仅凭一只棋子进攻，无法突破黑方在王翼的兵防线。白方所选的计划不切实际，构想也不够具体。他应走21. g4；若21... Nf7，则22. Qg3。此后可能出现22... h6 23. h4 a5 24. Rf2 a4 25. Rg1 axb3 26. axb3 Ra2 27. g5! hxg5 28. hxg5 Rxc2 29. Rh2 fxg5 30. Qh3 Nh6 31. Rxg5，白方制造出多种威胁。

**21... Be8**

text: The move Ng6 threatens nothing, if, of course, Black does not accept the sacrifice, and therefore it was possible, without losing time, to play 21... a5. Sometimes the choice of a move can be explained by the style of a chessplayer. And Danushevsky was an extraordinarily careful chessplayer, who never missed an opportunity to strengthen his lines of defence, even if there was no direct need for this.
zh: 只要黑方不接受弃子，Ng6就没有实际威胁，因此黑方本可直接走21... a5，节省时间。有时，棋手选择某步棋的原因可以从其风格中找到。达努舍夫斯基是一位极其谨慎的棋手，即使并无迫切需要，也从不错过加固防线的机会。

text: Now even Danushevsky pays no attention to White's attack. His plan is build on sand.
zh: 现在，就连达努舍夫斯基也不再理会白方的进攻了。白方的计划犹如沙上建塔，根本没有坚实基础。

text: White still cherishes the hope of playing after 24... axb3 25. axb3 Ra2 26. Ng6 Rf7? 27. Rxh7 or 26... Bxg6 27. fxg6 h6 28. Qe6+ Kh8 29. b4! With his reply, Black destroys even this modest hope, after which the crowd of White pieces on the king's flank proves to be absolutely useless.
zh: 白方仍寄希望于24... axb3 25. axb3 Ra2 26. Ng6 Rf7? 27. Rxh7，或者26... Bxg6 27. fxg6 h6 28. Qe6+ Kh8 29. b4!。然而，黑方接下来的应手连这点希望也打破了；此后，白方聚集在王翼的子力将完全无所作为。

text: Convinced of the failure of his plan of attack, Evtifeev begins a retreat on all lines and hurries to transfer his pieces back from the king's flank. Meanwhile Black seizes the initiative and invades the enemy camp along the a-file.
zh: 叶夫季费耶夫认清进攻计划已经失败，开始全线撤退，急忙把子力从王翼调回。与此同时，黑方夺得主动，沿a线侵入白方阵地。

text: 24... Qd7! 25. Qg3 axb3 26. axb3 Ra2 27. Qe1
zh: 24... Qd7! 25. Qg3 axb3 26. axb3 Ra2 27. Qe1

text:
Nothing was offered by 27. Ng6 Bxg6 28. fxg6 h6 29. Bg4 Qe7. 

**27... Qa7 28. Rf3 Bf7 29. Rf1 Ra8 30. Nf3**
zh:
27. Ng6 Bxg6 28. fxg6 h6 29. Bg4 Qe7也不能给白方带来任何好处。

**27... Qa7 28. Rf3 Bf7 29. Rf1 Ra8 30. Nf3**

text: White's pieces return to the same positions from where they began the offensive ten moves ago! He has succeeded in avoiding material loss, but in return the positional losses he has suffered are serious. Black has opened and captured the a-file, his rook has invaded on a2, he threatens... c4 and the extending of the invasion along the second rank.
zh: 白方的棋子竟又回到了十步前开始进攻时的位置！他虽然避免了子力损失，却在局面上蒙受了严重损失。黑方已经打开并占据a线，车侵入a2，接下来威胁...c4，并将侵入范围扩展到第二横线。

text:
Systematic, but a rather slow way of realising the advantage. More energetic was 31... c4 32. bxc4 bxc4 33. Rb1 Qc3 34. Ne1 cxd3, or 33. g4 Rb8 34. Ra1 Rbb2.

**32. g4**
zh:
这种兑现优势的方法有条不紊，却稍嫌缓慢。更有力的是31... c4 32. bxc4 bxc4 33. Rb1 Qc3 34. Ne1 cxd3；或者33. g4 Rb8 34. Ra1 Rbb2。

**32. g4**

text: White hurls himself into the attack 11 moves late and in far worse conditions than on the 21st move, but this is his last and only chance of saving himself. As they say, better late than never.
zh: 白方终于投入进攻，但已经晚了11步，条件也比第21步时差得多。不过，这是他最后、也是唯一的自救机会。正所谓亡羊补牢，犹未为晚。

text: A colourful and instructive scene of invasion!
zh: 这是一幅生动而富有启发性的重子侵入图景！

text: 34. gxf6 gxf6 35. Ne1
zh: 34. gxf6 gxf6 35. Ne1

text: White counts on sharpening the game by Bh5.
zh: 白方打算用Bh5使局面变得尖锐。

text: One of those unfortunate mistakes, which is usually provoked by too great tension of struggle. After 36. Bh5 Black would still have experienced some trouble.
zh: 这种令人惋惜的错误，往往是斗争过于紧张所致。如果走36. Bh5，黑方仍会遇到一些麻烦。

text:
Thus, if 36... Bxb3, then 37. Qg4 and White, threatening Rg1, obtains an attack. Nevertheless even the attempt 36. Bh5 would prove unsuccessful, if Black were to then simply continue 36... c4 37. Bxf7 Nxf7 38. bxc4 bxc4 39. dxc4 Qe3, winning the e4 pawn and the game. 

**36... Bxb3!**
zh:
例如36... Bxb3 37. Qg4，白方威胁Rg1，能够获得攻势。不过，只要黑方简单地走36... c4 37. Bxf7 Nxf7 38. bxc4 bxc4 39. dxc4 Qe3，就能吃掉e4兵并获胜，因此36. Bh5这一尝试最终也不能成功。

**36... Bxb3!**

text: White overlooked this reply. On 37. cxb3 follows 37... Rxe2, threatening mate in one move.
zh: 白方漏算了这步应手。若37. cxb3，则37... Rxe2，威胁一步杀。

text:
So as, on 37... Bxc2, to reply 38. Qg4. 

**37... Nxe4!**
A beautiful and decisive blow. Nf2+ is threatened.
zh: 漂亮而决定性的一击，威胁...Nf2+。

text: 38. dxe4
zh: 38. dxe4

text:
White also has at his disposal the move 38. Qf3, but after 38... Bd5! 39. dxe4 Qxf3+ 40. Bxf3 Bc6, despite the extra piece he remains powerless against the threatening avalanche of Black pawns on the queen's flank, for example 41. Rg2 c4 42. Kg1 b4 43. Kf1 b3 44. cxb3 Rxg2 45. Bxg2 c3 etc. 

**38... Bxc2 39. Nxc2 Rxc2 40. Rxc2 Qxc2 41. Qxc2 Rxc2**
zh:
白方还可以走38. Qf3，但38... Bd5! 39. dxe4 Qxf3+ 40. Bxf3 Bc6之后，尽管白方多一子，却仍无力抵挡黑方后翼兵群的汹涌攻势。例如41. Rg2 c4 42. Kg1 b4 43. Kf1 b3 44. cxb3 Rxg2 45. Bxg2 c3等。

**38... Bxc2 39. Nxc2 Rxc2 40. Rxc2 Qxc2 41. Qxc2 Rxc2**

text: An endgame is reached in which Black's three connected passed pawns leave White no hope. He resists for a few more moves out of inertia.
zh: 进入残局后，黑方三个相连的通路兵使白方毫无希望。白方只是惯性地又抵抗了几步。

text: 42. Rb1 b4 43. Bd1 d3 44. Kg1 Ke7 45. h3 Kd6 46. Kf1 Kc6 47. Rb3 Rc3 48. Ke1 Kb5 49. Kd2 Rxb3 50. Bxb3 c4 0-1
zh: 42. Rb1 b4 43. Bd1 d3 44. Kg1 Ke7 45. h3 Kd6 46. Kf1 Kc6 47. Rb3 Rc3 48. Ke1 Kb5 49. Kd2 Rxb3 50. Bxb3 c4 0-1

text: In this most complicated and interesting game one circumstance attracts our attention. Black's most serious mistake, which might have led to his defeat, was the 13th move... d4, and yet it is precisely the d4 pawn which is the cornerstone of his successful pawn advance on the queen's flank! Thus, because of the changing situation on the board, a bad move is converted into just the opposite. This is one of the manifestations of dialectics, organically inherent in chess.
zh: 这盘极其复杂而有趣的对局中，有一点值得注意。黑方最严重、原本可能导致输棋的错误是13... d4，但后来恰恰是这个d4兵，成为黑方后翼冲兵得以成功的基石！可见，随着棋盘上形势的变化，一步坏棋的作用也可能转向相反的一面。这正是国际象棋内在辩证性的一种体现。

text: We look at one more game, perhaps the most brilliant illustration of play on the a-file, and the dangerous consequence ensuing from an invasion on it with heavy pieces.
zh: 再看一盘棋。它或许是a线作战最精彩的范例，也鲜明展示了让对手重子沿a线侵入会带来怎样危险的后果。

text: English Opening
zh: 英国式开局

text: White: M.Yudovich
zh: 白方：M. 尤多维奇

text: Black: V.Alatortsev
zh: 黑方：V. 阿拉托尔采夫

text: (Semi-final, 14th USSR Championship 1944)
zh: （第14届苏联锦标赛半决赛，1944年）

text: 1. c4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 d6 5. d4 Be7 6. Be2 O-O 7. O-O Re8 8. b3 Bg4 9. Bb2 Bf8 10. h3 Bh5
zh: 1. c4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 d6 5. d4 Be7 6. Be2 O-O 7. O-O Re8 8. b3 Bg4 9. Bb2 Bf8 10. h3 Bh5

text: Strictly speaking, for the present, both opponents still have no real, contemplated plans. They manoeuvre with circumspection, attempting to concentrate the action of the pieces and pawns around the central squares, and are guided in their actions by rough considerations.
zh: 严格说来，双方此时都还没有真正经过深思熟虑的计划。他们谨慎调动子力，试图把棋子和兵的作用集中到中心格附近，行棋仍以概括性的考虑为依据。

text: Carried away by manoeuvering, White overlooks the loss of a pawn.
zh: 白方专注于调动子力，却没有注意到自己可能丢兵。

text:
The pawn is won in this way: 11... Bxf3 12. Bxf3 (in order to save the pawn, it is necessary to play 12. gxf3, but, after 12... exd4 13. exd4 Nh5, Black has an advantage which is worth more than a pawn) 12... exd4 13. exd4 Rxe1+ 14. Qxe1 Nxd4 15. Bxb7 Nc2 16. Qd1 Nxa1 17. Bxa8 Nxb3. However it is very difficult to capitalise on this gain after 18. Nd5! Nxd5 19. Bxd5 Nc5 20. Bd4. It is possible that Black, not wishing to be content with a draw, deliberately rejected this variation, intending to create a potentially weak square on d3 and limit the activity of the bishop b2. This is still not a plan, but already preparatory action for the plan. 

**12. Nh2 Bxe2 13. Qxe2 d5!**
zh:
黑方可以这样得兵：11... Bxf3 12. Bxf3（若想保住这兵，就必须走12. gxf3，但12... exd4 13. exd4 Nh5之后，黑方获得的优势比一兵更有价值）12... exd4 13. exd4 Rxe1+ 14. Qxe1 Nxd4 15. Bxb7 Nc2 16. Qd1 Nxa1 17. Bxa8 Nxb3。不过，18. Nd5! Nxd5 19. Bxd5 Nc5 20. Bd4之后，这点收获很难转化为胜势。黑方可能不愿满足于和棋，因而主动放弃这一变化，转而设法使d3成为潜在弱格，并限制b2象的活动。这还不算完整的计划，但已经是在为计划作准备。

**12. Nh2 Bxe2 13. Qxe2 d5!**

text: White's queen's bishop is now seriously cramped, Black has succeeded in organising a strong pawn outpost in the centre on e4, the position of his pieces is obviously better, the manoeuvre... Nb4-d3, with the establishment of the knight on the weak square, is threatened. The principal events, however, must take place in the centre.
zh: 白方的后翼象现在受到严重限制；黑方则在中心e4建立起坚强的兵据点，子力配置明显更好，并威胁通过...Nb4-d3把马安置到弱格上。不过，斗争的焦点仍应在中心。

text: The d5 square - this is the point to which the attention of the opponents must be riveted. The d5 pawn supports the e4 pawn, and if Black succeeds in playing... c6 after removing the knight from that square, then this would considerably strengthen his central pawn group. Consolidation of the centre and an invasion on d3 - this is the content of the first stage of Black's plan. From this follows White's next task: to prevent this intention of the opponent. He can increase his influence over the d5 point by the move 14. Ng4.
zh: d5格才是双方必须紧盯的要点。d5兵支撑着e4兵；黑方若能先移开c6马，再走...c6，就能大大巩固中心兵群。巩固中心并侵入d3，是黑方计划第一阶段的内容。由此也就明确了白方眼前的任务：阻止对手的这一意图。白方可以14. Ng4加强对d5的控制。

text: Since... dxc4 would be a violation of Black's whole plan, there remains 14... Nxg4, on which there are at least 3 continuations for White - Qxg4, hxg4 and cxd5, leading to complicated variations in which the opponent would have to solve a series of new problems, for example 15. Qxg4 Ne7 16. cxd5 f5 17. Qe2 Nxd5 18. Qc4 c6 19. Rac1 etc.
zh: 由于...dxc4会违背黑方的整体计划，黑方只好走14... Nxg4。此时，白方至少有Qxg4、hxg4和cxd5三种后续手段，都能引出复杂变化，迫使对手解决一系列新的问题。例如15. Qxg4 Ne7 16. cxd5 f5 17. Qe2 Nxd5 18. Qc4 c6 19. Rac1等。

text:
Even 14. a3, barring the way of the Black knight to d3, with the possible continuation 14... Na5 15. Qc2 dxc4 16. bxc4 Nxc4 17. Nxe4 Nxb2 18. Nxf6+ Qxf6 19. Qxb2 Qb6 20. Qc3, would be better than what happens in the game. 

**14. Rad1**
zh:
即使走14. a3，阻断黑马前往d3的路线，也比实战下法好。可能的后续手段是14... Na5 15. Qc2 dxc4 16. bxc4 Nxc4 17. Nxe4 Nxb2 18. Nxf6+ Qxf6 19. Qxb2 Qb6 20. Qc3。

**14. Rad1**

text: A planless move, not pursuing any kind of objective and not guided by a concrete idea. Furthermore it is unsatisfactory because it does not prevent the penetration of the Black knight to the weak d3 square.
zh: 这步棋没有计划，既不追求明确目标，也没有具体构想指导。更令人不满的是，它未能阻止黑马侵入d3弱格。

text: But what guided White in making his last move? It seems he simply decided to transfer the rook from the corner square a1, where it is inactive, to an undoubtedly better central square d1.
zh: 那么，白方为什么走这一步呢？看来，他只是想把车从无所作为的角落a1格，调到位置无疑更好的中央d1格。

text: There will be positions (particularly in the opening stage) in which such a method of activity, based on general considerations, is fully justified. However, even in strictly positional conditions, there is usually sufficient material for a concrete play, for the performing and completion of a task based on the calculation of variations. This applies wholly to the present game.
zh: 在某些局面中，尤其是开局阶段，根据一般性考虑这样行棋完全合理。不过，即使在纯粹的局面性斗争中，通常也有足够的具体内容，可以据此计算变化、确定任务并付诸实施。眼前这盘棋正是如此。

text: White's position is considerably worse, but the main thing is that he has no prospects at all with the presence of the knight in the very centre of his army. Therefore a courageous solution would be to sacrifice the exchange 18. Rxd3 exd3 19. Qd1. The splinter would be removed and White could put up a stubborn resistance. Instead of this he prefers to drag on a miserable existence.
zh: 白方局面已明显较差，更严重的是，黑马深入其子力配置的腹地，使他几乎无计可施。因此，勇敢的选择应是弃半子：18. Rxd3 exd3 19. Qd1。这样可以拔掉这根刺，争取顽强抵抗的机会。实战中，白方却宁愿继续困守苦境。

text:
With the intention of exchanging the only piece capable of ousting the knight from d3, and thereby securing himself the "eternal" knight. And yet better was 20... b6 or... Qa5. 

**21. Qc2?**
zh:
黑方打算换掉唯一能把马赶出d3的棋子，从而确保这匹马成为铁马。不过，20... b6或20... Qa5仍然更好。

**21. Qc2?**

text:
But it is difficult to leave this move without a question mark. White again ignores the opponent's intention and plays without a plan. 21. Na4 was necessary, with the threat Nb2. In the event of 21... Ba3 follows 22. Nc5! Nxc5 23. dxc5 Bxc5 24. cxd5 cxd5 25. Kh1 with the dangerous threat Qb2. If, however, on 21. Na4, Black replies 21... b6, then White all the same exchanges the invading knight by 22. Nb2. This is why Black should have played... b6 on the 20th move, so as not to allow the move Nc5.

**21... Bxc3**
zh:
这步棋实在不能不打问号。白方再次无视对手的意图，毫无计划地行棋。应走21. Na4，威胁Nb2。若21... Ba3，则22. Nc5! Nxc5 23. dxc5 Bxc5 24. cxd5 cxd5 25. Kh1，白方制造出Qb2的危险威胁。若黑方以21... b6回应21. Na4，白方仍可22. Nb2，换掉侵入的黑马。这也解释了为什么黑方应在第20步就走...b6，不给白方Nc5的机会。

**21... Bxc3**

text: After this exchange, White's game can hardly be saved.
zh: 这次交换之后，白方的局面已很难挽救。

text: Opening the c-file is favourable only for Black, who without difficulty will occupy it with his rooks.
zh: 打开c线只对黑方有利，因为黑方可以轻易用双车占据这条线。

text: Pinning down the b3 pawn, which is important for the execution of the plan of attack on the a-file.
zh: 固定住b3兵。这对实施a线进攻计划十分重要。

text: Beginning the carrying out of the second stage of the plan - to open the a-file. White cannot prevent this and his only chance of resistance is to organise an attack on the king's flank. A small, though clearly insufficient prerequisite for this is, for example, the move g4.
zh: 黑方开始实施计划的第二阶段：打开a线。白方无法阻止，唯一的抵抗机会是在王翼组织进攻。走g4等手段为此提供了一点可能，但显然还远远不够。

text: And so it is: White tries his last chance.
zh: 果然如此，白方开始尝试最后的机会。

text: Black will combine active play on the queen's flank with necessary prophylactics on the king's. This presents no difficulties since the threats are very modest. Now Black himself threatens to take on g4.
zh: 黑方将在后翼积极行动，同时在王翼采取必要的预防措施。由于白方的威胁很有限，这并不困难。现在，黑方自己反而威胁吃掉g4兵。

text: 26. gxf5 Qxf5 27. Kh2 Re7
zh: 26. gxf5 Qxf5 27. Kh2 Re7

text: Another advantage for Black should be noted: the seventh and eighth ranks, present themselves as splendid routes for transfer of the rooks from one edge of the board to the other, allow him to very forcefully exploit the powerful activity of these mobile pieces. This freedom and speed of manoeuvre in his own rear along the open ranks can sometimes prove to be a decisive factor. White, in this respect, finds himself in a far worse situation. On the first rank there is a dense crowd of his own pieces, the second is also jammed since, on each of these lines, the knight, established on d3, takes away two squares. Below we will see how well Black exploits the advantage of his control of White's “rear".
zh: 黑方还有一个优势值得注意：第七、第八横线为双车在棋盘两翼之间调动提供了绝佳通道，使黑方能够充分发挥车强大的机动性。利用己方后方畅通的横线自由而迅速地调车，有时可以成为决定性因素。白方在这方面的处境差得多：第一横线上子力拥挤，第二横线也交通不畅，因为占据d3的黑马在这两条横线上各控制着两个格。接下来可以看到，黑方如何充分利用对方后方受制的弱点。

text: It is necessary to prevent the invasion of the White rook on g5.
zh: 必须阻止白车侵入g5。

text: 29. Rd2 Kh7 30. Rdg2 a4! 31. Bh4
zh: 29. Rd2 Kh7 30. Rdg2 a4! 31. Bh4

text: Of course, not 31. Rxg6 in view of 31... Nxe1 (or 31... Qxg6 32. Rxg6 Nxe1!).
zh: 当然不能31. Rxg6，因为黑方有31... Nxe1，或31... Qxg6 32. Rxg6 Nxe1!。

text: 31... axb3 32. axb3 Rea7
zh: 31... axb3 32. axb3 Rea7

text: Beginning a typical process of invasion and also the realisation of it - a flank attack on the king's position.
zh: 典型的侵入过程开始了，随后便要把侵入转化为具体成果：从侧面进攻白王的位置。

text: It seems that White has finally created a real threat - Rxg6.
zh: 白方似乎终于制造了一个实实在在的威胁：Rxg6。

text: What for? After 34. Qg4 the struggle could be continued, but now the end approaches surprisingly quickly: the final scene of the White army, completely taken captive, is rather colourful and characteristic for an attack from the flank.
zh: 这步棋有什么用呢？34. Qg4之后尚可继续斗争，实战却迅速走向终局。最后，白方全军被牢牢困住，景象鲜明而生动，充分体现了从侧面进攻的特点。

text: Realisation! The harmonious activity of the Black rooks switches from the a-file to the first rank. (see next diagram)
zh: 现在开始兑现优势！黑方双车协调配合，作战方向由a线转向第一横线。（见下图）

text: On 42. Rh2 could follow 42... Rf3+ 43. Kg2 Rb1 winning the queen. However, here there is already more than one way to victory.
zh: 若42. Rh2，则42... Rf3+ 43. Kg2 Rb1，黑方得后。不过，此时黑方已经不止一种获胜方法。

text: Though we have given special attention to the breakthrough of heavy pieces on the a-file, it is clear that its planning, technique and results are not very much different from the breakthrough into the position of the enemy army on other files. Of course, there is some difference, particularly in the process of the realisation of the invasion, between the course of the struggle with a breakthrough along the edge-file and the central e or d lines. In the latter case, the rooks which break through have to operate in the direction of both flanks, and at times this can even weaken the strength of the breakthrough.
zh: 本章着重讨论重子沿a线突破，但显然，这种突破在计划、实施方法和结果上，与沿其他线侵入敌方阵地并无太大差别。当然，沿边线突破与沿中央的e线或d线突破，仍存在一些区别，尤其是在将侵入转化为成果的过程中。沿中央线突破时，侵入的车需要兼顾两翼，有时反而会分散突破的力量。

text: However, upon an invasion along the edge-file, the attack of the rooks is launched in the direction of one flank and therefore becomes, as it were, more concrete and strong.
zh: 沿边线侵入时，车的进攻则集中朝向一翼，因此目标更明确，力量也更集中。
